plan: [ This two-stage format is strategically equivalent to a sealed-bid second-price auction: the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid. For risk-neutral bidders with independent private values, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Underbidding risks losing positive surplus when the price is below my value; overbidding risks paying above value. With no useful history (1 round), I will bid my value exactly to maximize expected profit. ]

[ This mechanism pays the second-highest sealed bid and awards to the highest sealed bid, equivalent to a Vickrey (second-price) auction. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true private value: overbidding risks negative profit if the second-highest exceeds your value; underbidding forfeits positive surplus when you could have won cheaply. There’s no useful history (round 1 of 1), and values are independent. To maximize long-run/expected profit, bid truthfully. With value $6, set exit at 6. ]

[ This is strategically equivalent to a second‑price (Vickrey) auction: the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid. The dominant strategy is to bid my true value to maximize expected profit. Overbidding risks paying above value if others overbid; underbidding risks losing profitable wins when the final price would be below my value. There is no multi-round learning here (1 round), so no value in strategic shading. Therefore, I will bid my private value exactly: 17. ]
